entityDescription:
The Faculty of Telecommunications at the Technical University of Sofia is the nation's premier hub for engineering innovation in the Information and Telecommunication field. We don't just keep pace with the digital world; we build networks that connect it. 
The Bachelor's curriculum provides elective courses for further specialization in radiocommunications, audio and video technologies, telecommunications networks and technologies, and communication systems management.

Focus on the unique challenges of transmitting ultra-high-definition, low-latency 3D content, and developing the systems that will power the next generation of telepresence, gaming, and virtual collaboration.
Telecommunications is one of the most modern and dynamically developing fields of engineering and technology today, characterized by significant investments, the presence of leading global technology companies. entityDescription:

The company combines two core products: the ONE - a polymer SLS printer with integrated post-print annealing at a fraction of incumbent pricing - and TRACE - a manufacturing intelligence platform that automates traceability, parameter selection, and quality documentation across additive manufacturing workflows.

Target sectors include space hardware manufacturers, satellite and launch vehicle teams, defence, automotive, and industrial R&D - any environment where part quality, traceability, and supply chain independence are non-negotiable.

description:
VYRONIS Technologies Ltd
Sector: Space Biotech • AI & Radiation Biology • Astronaut Health
Location: Glasgow, Scotland
Founder: Varun Cruz
Overview 
VYRONIS Technologies is a space biotechnology company developing radiation-adaptive bio-AI systems to enhance astronaut health, radiation resilience, and biological safety in deep-space missions. The company’s flagship platform, GENORA™, integrates radiobiological data, molecular AI, and predictive genomics to model how living systems adapt to ionising radiation; enabling early detection, intervention, and countermeasure design for spaceflight and nuclear medicine environments. 
ESA BIC Focus 
Through the ESA Business Incubation Centre UK, VYRONIS is advancing the GENORA™ Translational Framework (TRL 3–7) — combining laboratory data, in-silico simulations, and microgravity-exposed biological datasets. The aim is to produce adaptive bio-AI algorithms that can predict and mitigate radiation damage for astronauts, satellites, and terrestrial healthcare systems. Vision To pioneer a new era of bio-adaptive intelligence for human space exploration — ensuring every mission beyond Earth is powered by biologically informed, AI-driven health resilience. Applications Space Health: Predictive modelling for astronaut exposure and countermeasure optimisation. Terrestrial Medicine: Radiotherapy safety, oncology insights, and emergency-response biotechnologies. Dual-Use AI Systems: Algorithms for defence, nuclear energy, and planetary colonisation research. 
Key Partners 
ESA BIC UK (incubation support) 
Innovate UK (funding) 
Academic collaborations with UK and EU research institutions

description:
SI Robotics is a Warsaw-based deep-tech company developing sovereign European humanoid and robotic systems for industrial, defence, and space applications. We are a Physical-AI-first company, integrating advanced actuators, tendon-based joints, and compliant control systems with reinforcement-learning frameworks to create embodied intelligence for the physical world.

Our mission is to advance Physical AI — the fusion of mechanical design, sensing, and neural control that allows robots to understand, interact with, and adapt to their environment with human-like precision. We believe this domain will define the next generation of autonomy across terrestrial and orbital contexts.

Within the space sector, SI Robotics develops lightweight, ECSS-compliant actuator systems for robotic arms, EVA/IVA assistance, and on-orbit servicing. Our modular joint architecture and torque-controlled drives are designed to operate under the mechanical, radiation, and thermal constraints of space environments.

We are fully aligned with European AI, data, and machinery regulations (including the 2027 AI Act and Machinery Regulation). SI Robotics’ architecture ensures full traceability, explainability, and data sovereignty, making our Physical AI stack natively compliant with EU ethical and legal frameworks — a key differentiator from non-EU robotics providers.

SI Robotics contributes to the emerging European Physical AI policy agenda, supporting ESA and the European Commission in building safe, transparent, and sovereign autonomy for robotic systems. We work closely with research institutions and industrial partners to develop embodied AI models that meet dual-use and security-sensitive requirements, ensuring resilience and interoperability across ESA, defence, and industry ecosystems.

entityDescription:
Mariborski vodovod is a regional public utility company responsible for supplying safe and healthy drinking water to the Municipality of Maribor and 15 surrounding municipalities in northeastern Slovenia. In addition to water supply, the company is also responsible for the operation and management of the Central Wastewater Treatment Plant Maribor, ensuring environmentally responsible and sustainable wastewater treatment for the wider region. With more than a century of tradition and extensive professional expertise, the company operates the largest water distribution network in Slovenia, managing 1.723 kilometers of pipelines and over 260 facilities. Each year, it supplies approximately 14 million cubic meters of drinking water to more than 160.000 residents.
The company’s vision is to be a modern, efficient, responsible, and innovative public utility that delivers top-quality services to its users, partners, and owners. Its core mission focuses on the long-term reliability of water sources, infrastructure, and service quality.
To improve efficiency and sustainability, Mariborski vodovod emphasizes the reduction of water losses, which currently stand at approximately 29%, with an Infrastructure Leakage Index (ILI) of 3.4, highlighting potential for further improvement. The water network is divided into 138 District Metered Areas (DMAs), enabling localized flow monitoring, faster leak detection, and targeted interventions.
Technologically advanced and innovation-driven, the company employs modern IT systems, including enterprise resource planning (ERP), geographic information systems (GIS), and SCADA industrial systems. It takes pride in its use of smart technologies, having installed 99.8% of smart meters, enabling accurate billing based on real consumption. Around 260 control meters and sensors throughout the network provide continuous monitoring, while the integration of GIS with a business intelligence (BI) system supports effective management through detailed dashboards and analytics.
Corporate social responsibility is embedded in the company’s operations, encouraging all employees, from staff to leadership, to contribute to sustainable and socially responsible strategies. Mariborski vodovod continuously invests in system modernization, reduces water and energy losses, promotes innovation, and builds a motivated, highly skilled workforce. Through efficient, rational business practices and a process-based organization, the company ensures long-term financial stability while maintaining a strong focus on customer satisfaction, high-quality service, and open, responsive communication.
